articles.title: # 🔐 Gitleaks: Detect Secrets Before They Reach Git
articles.excerpt: Have you ever accidentally committed an API key, database password, or access token to Git? 😬 A single mistake can expose sensitive credentials in a repository. Even if you remove the secret in the n…
articles.body: Have you ever accidentally committed an API key, database password, or access token to Git? 😬 A single mistake can expose sensitive credentials in a repository. Even if you remove the secret in the next commit, it may remain in Git history, forks, clones, or CI/CD logs. Gitleaks is an open-source secret-scanning tool that helps developers detect potentially exposed credentials in Git repositories and files. In this article, we'll explore how Gitleaks works, how to install it on Ubuntu, its pros and cons, real-world applications, and how to integrate it into a GitLab CI/CD pipeline. 🚀 1. What Is Gitleaks?

articles.title: A bug in my own branch-guard hook, caught by typing one extra space
articles.excerpt: A bug in my own branch-guard hook, caught by typing one extra space Context: Last week I shipped a set of 4 Claude Code hooks that catch common agent mistakes — no-op edits, pushes to the wrong branch…
articles.body: A bug in my own branch-guard hook, caught by typing one extra space Context: Last week I shipped a set of 4 Claude Code hooks that catch common agent mistakes — no-op edits, pushes to the wrong branch, out-of-scope writes, and unverified claims at the end of a turn. I wrote about them in article #1 and the testing in #2 . This piece is the small, embarrassing follow-up: a bug I found by dog-fooding the hooks on their own payloads. The hook block-wrong-branch.sh runs on PreToolUse(Bash) for git push . It extracts the target branch and matches it against .claude/branch-policy.json . Simplified: # Only inspect git push commands. case " $command " in * "git push" * | * "git push" * ) : ;; * ) exit 0 ;; esac # Tokens after "git push".

articles.title: PunyGuard: A Chrome Extension That Blocks Every Internationalized Domain
articles.excerpt: аррӏө.com and apple.com. Put them side by side: can you tell which one is real? All five letters in the first one are Cyrillic. Even so, Chrome 154's address bar displayed it exactly as-is. It looks i…
articles.body: аррӏө.com and apple.com . Put them side by side: can you tell which one is real? All five letters in the first one are Cyrillic. Even so, Chrome 154's address bar displayed it exactly as-is. It looks identical to apple.com ( GIZMODO article ). After reading that article, I built a small Chrome extension called PunyGuard . It blocks access to internationalized domain names (IDNs), all of them, no exceptions. It doesn't judge whether a domain looks similar to anything. Legitimate Japanese domains get blocked too. It may look like a heavy-handed tradeoff, but that tradeoff is the core of the design. Out of nowhere, a confession: I don't like Japanese domain names.

A full abstraction layer that routes across several gateways is usually the wrong choice. A multi-gateway layer pays off only under a few specific business conditions, and it costs far more to own than the whiteboard diagram suggests. You may be a CTO or founder, and someone in a planning meeting just said "we can't be locked into one payment provider". If so, this is for you. The worry is fair. articles.title: The 10 Best Low Fantasy Books
articles.excerpt: From Neil Gaiman to Haruki Murakami, these are the most fascinating low fantasy books that treat the ordinary as something extarordinary.
articles.body: Fantasy is a broad genre of fiction, and low fantasy might be one of its most slippery corners. The term can describe anything from stories where magic barely exists — like Game of Thrones — to tales in which the supernatural quietly intrudes on an otherwise recognizable world, akin to Pan’s Labyrinth . Unlike high fantasy, which often transports readers to entirely invented worlds with their own mythologies, low fantasy finds the extraordinary lurking just beneath the surface of the familiar.

articles.title: 34 Years Later, the Best-Ever 'Far Side' Quote Will Still Leave You Speechless
articles.excerpt: Gary Larson's comic strip The Far Side was known for its visual humor, but this is the best-ever quote from the series
articles.body: Larson didn’t do deep . He didn’t do inspirational. Many of his cartoons required you to think, but not because they were thoughtful in the lofty sense. They required thought because Larson’s work was brilliant, and you sometimes had to figure out what the punchline was. For example, this comic strip where an artist is painting a woman as a half-fly creature. You likely see the woman or the painting first, and you wonder why the artist is painting her that way. Only after inspecting the comic more closely do you see the dead fly on his glasses. Larson’s work often requires the reader to investigate something, but usually not in any kind of overly deep way.
articles.author: Brian VanHooker

articles.body: Every once in a while, I come across a line that feels bigger than the book that birthed it. Of course, there are classics with years of literary study behind them that speak volumes on the nature of society, technology, or the world writ large. But few are quite as elegant or as profoundly humanistic as the final moments of Arkady and Boris Strugatsky’s Roadside Picnic . The 1972 novel offers a very different kind of sci-fi ending than its myriad predecessors and successors.

articles.title: Targeted ads delivered 0-click exploits to install mercenary malware
articles.excerpt: The incident is likely 1st confirmation of mercenary spyware delivered by targeted ads.
articles.body: Researchers say that mercenary hackers laced ads with zero-click exploits that installed sophisticated malware on the devices of targeted individuals when they did nothing other than load a website or open an installed app. The finding, published Thursday by the University of Toronto’s Citizen Lab, said the incident is likely to be the first confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered through targeted ads. The attacks, which worked on iOS and Android devices, are particularly pernicious because they work without requiring any interaction from the target and are invisible unless users run special forensic hardware or software.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the 1st ever green star, a cosmic zombie just in time for Halloween
articles.excerpt: Imagine if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween. Scientists have discovered that our star may go green if it turns into a cosmic zombie after its death in billions of years.
articles.body: How awesome would it be if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween? It turns out that scientists have discovered that our star may indeed go green, but only billions of years from now after its death — and only if it then starts eating planets like a cosmic zombie. That's possible because scientists have discovered that white dwarfs, the type of stellar remnants sun-sized stars leave behind when they die, can actually take on a range of colors including green if they snack on their rocky planets like cosmic cannibals. For stellar scientists, the colors of stars have always been indicative of their temperatures. Cool stars look orange, while stars like the sun look white , and the hottest stars glow pale blue.

articles.title: NASA to Help Unlock Mysteries of Mars’ Moons in Upcoming Mission
articles.excerpt: NASA is playing an important role in JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) mission, to advance our understanding of Mars’ moons and build on the agency’s long his…
articles.body: NASA is playing an important role in JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) mission, to advance our understanding of Mars’ moons and build on the agency’s long history of exploring the Red Planet. The mission aims to characterize and determine the origin of Mars’ moons Phobos and Deimos and deliver a sample of Phobos to Earth. The MMX spacecraft is targeting launch from JAXA’s Tanegashima Space Center in Japan at 3:41 p.m. EDT on Monday, Oct. 19 (4:41 a.m. JST on Tuesday, Oct. 20). An artist’s concept of JAXA’s MMX spacecraft during its Mars’ orbit insertion. The Martian moon Phobos, which MMX will explore and sample, is in the background.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 15, 1997: NASA launches Cassini-Hugyens probe on 7-year voyage to Saturn
articles.excerpt: On this day in space! Oct. 15, 1997: NASA launches Cassini-Hugyens probe on 7-year voyage to Saturn
articles.body: On Oct. 15, 1997, NASA launched the Cassini spacecraft on a mission to explore Saturn and its moons. It lifted off aboard a Titan 4B rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. It took almost seven years for the Cassini spacecraft to reach Saturn , with the spacecraft entering orbit around the ringed planet in 2004. Another smaller spacecraft called Huygens hitched a ride with Cassini, and it landed on Saturn's moon Titan in 2005. Cassini spent 13 years studying the Saturn system up close, and the mission lasted about 20 years before coming to an epic grand finale on Sept. 15, 2017 . Running low on fuel, NASA chose to steer Cassini straight into Saturn's atmosphere, where the spacecraft was destroyed . NASA's Cassini spacecraft lifts off on Oct.
